note: Hormuz stayed shut through the window: IRGC re-closed it Jul 12, the US blockade resumed Jul 14, and large-ship transits were near zero by early September.
Gulf sulfur and ammonia flows stayed disrupted, but urea fell back near year-ago prices and the FAO food index rose only 1-2.5% y/y; India and Brazil added offsets.
Same stress as the Jul 13 episode: fertilizer inputs disrupted, food prices up only modestly (FAO index +2.5% y/y in August).
Ex-China dysprosium rose from 6.8x to 16.3x the China price in Q3 as buyers scrambled, but there was no new Chinese ban and no reported production stoppages.
China's PPI swung to +4.1% (June) then eased to +3.5-3.8%; anti-dumping cases kept coming, but no sector-wide overcapacity tariff and the yuan held steady.
